newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus police bar deputies from old parliament.
newsitem.headline: Belarus police bar deputies from old parliament.

text.p: Police on Thursday barred deputies from entering the main chamber of Belarus' old parliament, only allowing them access to collect their belongings.
President Alexander Lukashenko wants to shut the parliament following his resounding victory in a controversial referendum last weekend.
"The police are only letting us in to collect our things," liberal faction leader Stanislav Bogdankevich told Reuters.
"This marks the setting up of a junta through the falsification of the referendum results."
Belarus has had two rival parliaments since Sunday's referendum, in which voters granted Lukashenko sweeping powers to reshape the former Soviet republic's state institutions.

On Wednesday deputies backing the president formally abolished the old parliament amid rousing applause under Lukashenko's approving gaze and approved the formation of a new, 110-seat lower house. An upper house is also planned.
Lukashenko's supporters said he would try to remove several dozen deputies occupying the old parliament.
"The opposition will not leave. We will wait for the Belarussian people to wake up," Bogdankevich said.
Lukashenko is expected to sign the new constitution approved by the referendum at a ceremony on Thursday afternoon.

Members of the rump parliament say phone lines linking their chamber to the president and the government have been cut, but a Council of Europe delegation on Wednesday recognised the rump as the legal legislature.
It declared Lukashenko's referendum illegal and said the new constitution "fell short of minimum democratic standards".
Opposition deputies had expressed fear that Lukashenko might get them out by force, as in April 1995, when hunger-striking deputies were beaten as they were ejected from the chamber.
